claim: A complete community book-library Index.base file is published on GitHub with filters on folder, multiple table and cards views (All Books, Queue, Published, Series Cards, By Year, Current Year), formulas for cover image, rating, series, and reading-years.
quote:
filters:
  and:
    - file.folder.contains("Personal/Reading/Books")
    - file.ext != "base"
formulas:
  Title: link(file.path, title)
  Rating: if(rating == null, "N/A", ["⭐", rating.toString()].join(" "))
  Cover: image(cover)

claim: The same book base demonstrates a By-Year cards view filtering log entries by year and a Series Cards view that pulls book series via the contains-this-handle pattern, with image: cover, imageFit: contain, cardSize: 160.
quote:
- type: cards
    name: By Year
    filters:
      and:
        - file.folder == "Personal/Reading/Books/Read"
        - log.filter(value.status == "Read" && value.timestamp.year == this.title)
    image: cover
    imageFit: contain
    cardSize: 160

claim: Practical PKM's book-library recipe uses a folder-path filter on the Book Notes folder with three views: a default table, a primary cards view showing cover/author/rating/pages, and a filtered '5 Star Books' cards view (rating == 5).
quote: Only shows files where the file path begins with Book Notes... Cards View - Primary display with cover images, configured to show author, rating, and page number... 5 Star Books View - Filtered cards showing only books where the rating property is ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

claim: A reading-log recipe demonstrates the readDates pattern using array filtering: a Read-by-Year view applies the filter readDates.toString().contains('2025') and a formula readDates.filter(value.toString().contains('2025')) on book notes that have a shelf and series property.
quote: Read by year filter: Advanced filter using "where readDates.toString().contains('2025')"... Functions applied: image(cover), link(file.name, title), and readDates.filter(value.toString().contains("2025"))

claim: An Obsidian forum 'Share & showcase' template for project/task tracking standardises four frontmatter keys — status, passion (1–5), deadline (datetime), progress (0–100) — and groups columns into source / display (emoji + progress-bar formulas) / sort categories.
quote:
status: In Progress
passion: 5
deadline: 2025-08-19T12:51:00
progress: 60 ... status field includes default options: "To Do, In Progress, Focus, On Hold, Cancelled, Completed"

claim: A 'home base' tutorial provides two complete table-view base configs: a whole-vault Note Checklist (file.inFolder('') and file.ext=='md') and a Projects & Exams base filtering on tags containsAny('projects','exam') with a tags containsAny('task') refinement, plus priOrder + due-date sorting.

got.md's complete 2026 guide publishes copy-paste templates including a minimal Debug base (file.ext=='md', columns file.path/folder/tags/links, limit 50) and a People-CRM Meetings view filtering list(attendees).contains(this) with columns date/file.name/project.
quote:
views:
  - type: table
    name: Meetings for this person
    filters:
      and:
        - 'list(attendees).contains(this)'
    columns:
      - date
      - file.name
      - project
    limit: 200

claim: A meeting-notes recipe builds two bases off a Type=='Meeting' note schema with Attendees and Projects multi-link properties: an Attendee base filtering Type=='Meeting' AND Attendees.contains(this.file), and a Project base using Projects.contains(this.file).
quote: For Attendee Base: The filter condition should be: Type == "Meeting" AND Attendees.contains(this.file). For Project Base: The filter condition should be: Projects.contains(this.file) AND Type == "Meeting"

claim: A Dataview-to-Bases migration walkthrough provides a complete 'On This Day' base over Daily Notes using a date-arithmetic formula on file.name and a table view filtering formula.on_this_day.contains('True').
quote:
filters:
  or:
    - file.inFolder("Daily Notes")
formulas:
  on_this_day: if(date(file.name).month == "09", if(date(file.name).day == "28", if(date(file.name).year != "2025", "True", "False"), "False"), "False")

claim: The Obsidian TV Tracker plugin demonstrates a movie/TV media-log frontmatter shape — title, type, status (Watchlist/Watched/Complete/Incomplete/In Progress), priority, rating, dates, progress, external link — that is directly usable as a Bases source schema.
quote: Each Movie and TV show is saved as a markdown file in a folder of your choice, with each file containing YAML content which is used to display, filter and sort content... For watchlist entries, you should enter 'Watchlist' as the status

quote: a user created a Base of Bases with a Cards view using a formula property for cover images. The specific detail mentioned is that the "Cover Image" property uses the formula `file.basename + ".jpg"`

claim: A community recipe-database template tags notes with #🍽️/recipe and uses a multi-select ingredients property (curated from ~300 common ingredients via Metadata Menu) so ingredient-overlap queries are possible — directly portable to a Bases filter on ingredients.contains(...).
quote: FROM #🍽️/recipe WHERE ingredients FLATTEN ingredients as ings... utilizing the Metadata Menu plugin to enable multi-select ingredient properties sourced from a curated list of approximately 300 common cooking ingredients
